One assumption behind a published value, shown in the UI next to it.

Every model response carries the full list, so a user can see which numbers
are inputs they chose and which are defaults EpiRoute supplied.

BandedQuantity.description:
A central value with a low and a high bound.

The bounds are *scenario bounds*: they come from re-running the model at
the low and high ends of its uncertain inputs. They are not statistically
calibrated confidence intervals, and :attr:`band_basis` says so in words
that the UI displays verbatim (AGENTS.md section 10.2).

band_basis.description: How the bounds were produced, e.g. 'scenario range: under-reporting 2x-10x'. Not a confidence interval.
band_basis.title: Band Basis

Quantity.description:
A single number published together with how it was produced.

``value`` is ``None`` exactly when the inputs were insufficient; in that
case ``value_type`` is :attr:`ValueType.UNKNOWN` and ``unavailable_reason``
explains the gap. This invariant is enforced, which is what prevents a
missing input from being rendered as ``0``.
Quantity.title: Quantity

ResponseWarning.description:
A caveat attached to a response.

Collected into a ``warnings`` list that the UI renders next to the numbers,
so a limitation travels with the value it qualifies instead of living only
in the documentation.
ResponseWarning.title: ResponseWarning

UnavailableReason.description:
Why a value could not be produced.

Attached to every null numeric field so the UI can explain the gap instead
of showing a blank or a zero.
UnavailableReason.title: UnavailableReason

ValueType.description:
How a published number was produced.

The five categories are mutually exclusive and are surfaced verbatim in the
API and the UI legend.

Attributes:
    OBSERVED: Directly reported or measured by an identified source, used
        without transformation beyond unit conversion and ISO normalisation.
    ESTIMATED: Derived from observations by a documented procedure that
        introduces assumptions (an under-reporting multiplier, a gravity
        model prediction).
    MODELLED: Produced by an explicit mathematical model from other inputs
        (the Poisson importation probability, the branching-process
        establishment probability).
    SCENARIO: Produced under user-selected or deliberately extreme
        assumptions. Scenario values answer "what if", not "what is".
    UNKNOWN: Inputs were insufficient to produce a meaningful value.
ValueType.title: ValueType

info.description:
EpiRoute connects public-health outbreak reports to the global air-travel
network and publishes three *separate* quantities for a destination:

1. **Local presence** — is there evidence the pathogen is already there?
2. **Importation risk** — probability that at least one infected traveller
   arrives within a time horizon.
3. **Local establishment risk** — probability that an introduction leads to
   sustained local transmission.

Every numeric field carries a `value_type` of `observed`, `estimated`,
`modelled`, `scenario` or `unknown`. A value that cannot be computed is
returned as `null` with an `unavailable_reason` — never as `0`.

For situational awareness and education only. Not a diagnostic tool, not an
official forecast, and not a substitute for WHO or national travel guidance.
info.title: EpiRoute API

get.description:
Returns the three risk quantities for a destination, kept strictly separate:

* `presence` — whether a source report attributes grounded cases to this country.
  Flight connectivity is never an input.
* `importation` — probability that at least one infected traveller arrives within
  the horizon.
* `establishment` — probability that an introduction leads to sustained local
  transmission.

Every numeric field carries a `value_type`, and a field that cannot be computed is
`null` with an `unavailable_reason`. Bands are **scenario ranges**, not confidence
intervals; `band_basis` states how each was produced.
